summary:
The One-Day Saronic Islands Cruise lets you visit three Greek islands while keeping Athens as your base. Sail across the Saronic Gulf to Hydra, Poros and Aegina, with time ashore at each stop before continuing to the next island. The full-day format gives you a taste of island hopping without adding hotel nights or managing separate ferry reservations during your stay.
Transfers between your Athens hotel and the cruise departure point are handled by air-conditioned coach. A professional English-speaking guide accompanies the program, while entrance fees for scheduled visits are included, leaving the day focused on the cruise and its three island stops.

itinerary.text: Transfer from Athens to Port of Piraeus to embark on your Saronic Islands cruise. Visit Hydra for free time, shopping, or swimming, Poros for a short visit, and Aegina with an optional visit to the Temple of Aphaia. Lunch will be served on board during the cruise. Return to Athens in the evening and transfer to your hotel.

faqs.q: What is included in the Full Day Saronic Islands Cruise?
faqs.a: The Full Day Saronic Islands Cruise is a scenic day trip from Athens that visits some of the most beautiful islands in the Saronic Gulf. Depending on the cruise itinerary, guests typically visit Hydra, Poros, and Aegina while enjoying beautiful coastal views, onboard entertainment, and a relaxing day at sea.

faqs.q: How much does the Full Day Saronic Islands Cruise cost?
faqs.a: The cruise starts from €145 per person for the 2026 season. The price includes cruise transportation, onboard facilities, guided assistance, and selected services according to the package. Final pricing may vary depending on travel dates and availability.

faqs.q: How long does the Full Day Saronic Islands Cruise last?
faqs.a: The cruise lasts approximately 10 hours, departing from Athens in the morning and returning in the evening. It is one of the most popular day excursions for visitors looking to experience the Greek islands without changing hotels

faqs.q: Which islands are usually visited during the cruise?
faqs.a: Most Saronic Islands cruises visit Hydra, Poros, and Aegina. Each island offers its own unique character, from Hydra's car-free harbor and elegant architecture to Poros' charming waterfront and Aegina's rich history and local specialties.

faqs.q: Does the Full Day Saronic Islands Cruise include a guide?
faqs.a: Yes, English-speaking guides or cruise hosts are available throughout the excursion. They provide information about the islands, local history, and cruise schedule while assisting passengers during the trip.

faqs.q: Is this cruise suitable for first-time visitors to Greece?
faqs.a: Yes, the cruise is ideal for first-time visitors who want to experience Greek island life without taking longer ferry journeys. It provides an excellent introduction to the beauty and culture of the Greek islands in a single day.

faqs.q: How fit do I need to be for the cruise?
faqs.a: The physical difficulty is easy. Travelers should be comfortable walking around island ports, waterfront promenades, and town centers. Most visitors of all ages and fitness levels can comfortably participate.

faqs.q: What are the highlights of Hydra, Poros, and Aegina?
faqs.a: Hydra is famous for its picturesque harbor, traditional stone mansions, and absence of motor vehicles. Poros offers beautiful waterfront views, pine-covered hills, and a relaxed atmosphere. Aegina is known for its ancient Temple of Aphaia, charming town center, and world-famous pistachios.

faqs.q: What is the cancellation policy for the Full Day Saronic Islands Cruise?
faqs.a: You can generally cancel free of charge up to 24 to 48 hours before departure, depending on the cruise operator's policy. Cancellations made closer to departure may be subject to charges.

faqs.q: Why is the Full Day Saronic Islands Cruise one of the most popular day trips from Athens?
faqs.a: The cruise allows visitors to experience multiple Greek islands in a single day while enjoying beautiful sea views, island culture, and a relaxing atmosphere. It is a perfect option for travelers who want to add an island experience to their Athens stay without spending additional nights away from the city.
